content_text: this excerpt/theme -- the amount of room you give yourself on your bad habits -- appears small but is arguably the key determinant of how your life will play out. compounding, in all things, is a motherfucker. the counterpoint is "everything in moderation"... I suppose there is no objectively correct answer, but I have found the old masters, the Greeks etc, to be in confederacy on the idea of total abstinence > trying to check the momentum of "dangerous passions" (Seneca) personally, I don't think u can worship too much at the altar of self-discipline. there is no such thing...get used to people telling you "relax," "take it easy on yourself," and so on. all of that is part of the plan, part of the design, and really is axiomatic: if you want to achieve results other people can't, you have to hold yourself to standards that other people view as completely unreasonable... period.
